alignments.note: Impersonal δεῖ takes a bare *must*. The supplied *he* is the unexpressed subject of the infinitive ἔχειν and belongs there under rule 74, not to the finite verb governing it; δεῖ is third-person impersonal, so *he* is not its own inflection-licensed subject under rule 9. This matches 1TI.3.15, where δεῖ takes a bare *ought* and the supplied *men* goes to ἀναστρέφεσθαι — rule 24's habit within one chapter.
δέ realized by *Moreover*. Variant SBLGNT.1TI.3.7.v002 is underdetermined with the base among the permitted readings, so no textual question arises here (rule 12).

Intensifying καί with no English word of its own, *Moreover* answering to δέ. Decided on the English alone under rule 65's test; a reference comparison will report this as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.
Anarthrous noun with no supplied determiner.
Attributive adjective on its own English word.

The infinitive takes the lexical *have* together with its supplied subject *he*, which rule 74 makes a rule 7 helper on the infinitive whose subject it is; discontinuous around the modal under rule 15. Placing *he* on δεῖ is the competing reading and is what this correction refuses, rule 74 and 1TI.3.15's identical δεῖ + infinitive deciding against it.

Substantival article whose modifier is an adverb rather than a participle: it keeps the discontinuous *them … that* under rule 32's contrast clause, no verb standing to carry the relativizer, and the copula goes to the adverb.
ἔξωθεν is a lexeme whose own sense is *without*, which rule 84 names in terms (ἔξωθεν → *without were*, headed on *without*), and rule 53 gives the supplied copula to the adverbial predicate.
ἵνα μή rendered by the single word *lest* under rule 39; neither particle is realized separately, so the pair is one unit headed on the first particle.
Anarthrous noun with no supplied determiner.
Inflected verb with its English subject; head on the lexical verb under rules 9 and 17.
Anarthrous noun with a supplied determiner, which is a rule 7/51 helper on the noun.
Article carrying its case preposition, one unit headed on *the* (rules 17, 21).
Noun standing alone, its determiner having gone to the article.

review_notes: Corrected: the supplied subject *he* (t002) moved from δεῖ to the infinitive ἔχειν under rule 74, leaving δεῖ a bare *must*. The chapter's own 1TI.3.15 analyses the identical δεῖ + infinitive that way, giving δεῖ a bare *ought* and the supplied *men* to ἀναστρέφεσθαι, so rule 24 requires the same reading here.
Every s### and t### partitioned exactly once after the correction.
The `unrepresented` καί at s003 will be reported as a disagreement by a reference comparison; rule 65's English-side test is what decides it, *Moreover* answering to δέ.
τῶν ἔξωθεν follows rule 32's contrast clause rather than rule 22: the article keeps the discontinuous *them … that* and the adverb takes the supplied copula under rules 53 and 84.
